page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 60 GB of system memory, which yields 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The platform bundles 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage spread across two physical drives, offering direct, low-latency disk throughput without discrete GPU acceleration hardware.

The underlying architecture features 504 MB of shared L3 cache and per-core L2 caches of 2 MB, accompanied by advanced vector and matrix acceleration flags including Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. In benchmark assessments, this hardware yields top-tier single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2297.0 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 36.82 GB/sec. Multi-core operations and memory access metrics reside in the middle tier, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 18700.11 and uncached read bandwidth peaking at 132.61 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, bundling local NVMe storage alongside a 1:3.75 vCPU-to-memory ratio eliminates external disk latency penalties for I/O-bound processes. While not designed for high-density GPU acceleration or extreme memory footprinting, the instance provides dependable density for applications that combine sustained processor throughput with active scratch disks. Key workload fits include database engines, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD artifact building, text and compression pipelines, and intermediate ETL operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 60 GB of system memory, and 804 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage across two drives, with no bundled GPU accelerator. The processor incorporates 504 MB of L3 cache alongside AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Synthetic tests indicate top-tier single-core computational speed and single-threaded compression capability, accompanied by standard mid-range multi-core processing and memory bandwidth metrics. By pairing dedicated compute cores with high-speed local NVMe storage, this configuration balances processing power with rapid local I/O. It is well matched for transactional databases, Redis caching layers, software compilation tasks, static web backends, and lightweight CPU-driven inference pipelines.
